newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors seek jail for sacked minister.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors seek jail for sacked minister.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Thursday sought a six-year jail term for sacked defence minister Lee Yang-ho on the opening day of his trial on charges of bribery and leaking military secrets, a prosecution official said.
Lee was fired from the cabinet on October 17 and was arrested later that month.

He was formally indicted last month on charges of accepting 150 million won ($180,000) as part of payments made to a Korean-American arms dealer by the Daewoo group in connection with a military helicopter deal.
Lee was also charged with leaking details to the arms merchant of military plans to buy sophisticated electronics.

Prosecutors also demanded jail terms of two years each for Sok Chin-chol, former president of Daewoo Heavy Industries who now heads the group's car subsidiary in Poland, and Chung Ho-shin, one-time vice president of Daewoo Heavy.
The two are standing trial together with Lee.
